#JGSDF is participating in the US-Philippines-led Multinational Joint Exercise “ #Balikatan26” in Philippines from 20 APR to 8 MAY 2026. Through this exercise conducting trainings such as amphibious operations, anti-landing fire, and anti-ship combat, the JGSDF is enhancing its various capabilities and improving interoperability with partner nations.
LTG Tokunaga, Vice Chief of Staff, JGSDF, attended the opening ceremony and he paid a courtesy call on the Philippine Army Headquarters. Through discussions with LTG Nafarette, Commander of the Philippine Army, they shared the importance of strengthening cooperation between the Japanese and Philippine armies. Furthermore, LTG Tokunaga paid a courtesy call on the Embassy of Japan in Philippines and held talks with H.E. Mr. Endo, Ambassador. #BK26 #Balikatan #ShoulderToShoulder

GROUPS DEMAND ACCOUNTABILITY FROM AFP

Various human rights advocate organizations and progressive groups held a rally at the gates of Camp Aguinaldo along EDSA in Quezon City on Friday, calling for accountability from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP).

The protest came after an alleged armed encounter with insurgents in Toboso, Negros Occidental on April 19, which reportedly resulted in the deaths of farmers and civilians, including student leader Alyssa Alano, journalist RJ Ledesma and 17 others.

📸 The STAR/Miguel De Guzman

Related: https://t.co/5bH9YHRWfZ

SM and ARISE PH with Partners Aim to Accelerate Resilience by 2030

The ARISE Philippines 2026 Annual General Meeting led by Hans Sy, Chairman of SM Prime Holdings Executive Committee and Chairperson of ARISE PH, brought together key network members and partners to advance the national disaster resilience agenda, highlighted by the ceremonial launch of the new ARISE Philippines website. The event also introduced the ARISE Knowledge Management System: SkillsBuild by IBM, a new platform facilitated by the Asia Pacific College to strengthen technology-enabled resilience initiatives nationwide. The milestone gathering was supported by the Department of Interior and Local Government, Department of Science and Technology, DOST-PHIVOLCS and the Bureau of Fire Protection.

The Japanese government has deployed a team of disaster relief experts to support the ongoing response efforts in the Navotas landfill, where a massive fire broke out on April 10, affecting many communities in the area.

The Japan International Cooperation Agency said Friday the deployment follows the activation of the Japan Disaster Relief Operations after an assistance request from the Philippine government.

The incident at the 41-hectare landfill has raised public health concerns due to its scale and potential impact on Navotas City and surrounding communities in Metro Manila.

FULL STORY: https://t.co/llmB7WzGAX

PAHAYAG NG PAMAHALAANG LUNGSOD QUEZON

Nakikiramay ang Pamahalaang Lungsod Quezon sa mga pamilya ng mga nasawi sa road accident sa Barangay Payatas ngayong umaga, April 24, 2026.

Lulan ng police mobile ng Philippine National Police (PNP) ang mga Persons Under Police Custody (PUPC) na patungong Quezon City Jail.

Agad na rumesponde ang emergency at health personnel ng lungsod upang tugunan ang sitwasyon at matiyak ang agarang pag-alalay sa lahat ng biktima. Kaagad silang dinala sa mga kalapit na ospital upang mabigyan ng medikal na atensyon.

Sa kasamaang palad, lima sa mga PUPC ang nasawi, habang ang isa ay nananatiling nasa kritikal na kondisyon. Samantala, ang apat na pulis na nagsilbing escort ay kasalukuyang nagpapagaling.

Makakaasa ang mga naulilang pamilya na sasagutin ng Pamahalaang Lungsod ang kaukulang gastusin sa pagpapagamot, gayundin ang funeral at burial services para sa mga nasawi. Maglalaan din ang lungsod ng psychosocial support at counselling upang makatulong sa kanilang pagbangon sa gitna ng trahedyang ito.

Nakikipag-ugnayan na rin ang lokal na pamahalaan sa mga kinauukulang ahensya para sa masusing imbestigasyon, na pangungunahan ng PNP-NCRPO, upang matukoy ang buong detalye ng insidente at matiyak ang pananagutan kung kinakailangan.

Cloudflare “Suspected Misleading Website” Warning: What it actually means for BG Wealth Sharing

Here’s the exact warning page people are seeing when they click on BG Wealth Sharing / DSJ Exchange links:

This is not a glitch, a traffic issue, or some coordinated attack by “haters.”

Cloudflare displays this warning when a domain has been reported for potentially misrepresenting itself as a legitimate brand or service. While Cloudflare notes the claim hasn’t been fully validated due to limited information, the purpose of the warning is to protect users from risk.

The reason this keeps happening is simple.

BG Wealth Sharing and DSJ Exchange are constantly generating new, short-lived domains — often in large volumes — rather than operating from a stable, verifiable web presence. When domains are repeatedly flagged or reported, they are abandoned and replaced.

That is not how legitimate financial platforms operate.

There is also a broader context that promoters are deliberately ignoring.

Regulators across multiple jurisdictions have already issued warnings about BG Wealth Sharing and related operations. These include authorities in Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, New Zealand, the Philippines, Tonga, and Samoa. The concerns raised are consistent: potential investment fraud, misleading representations, and unlicensed activity.

The underlying model follows a familiar pattern.

Users are shown supposed “trading activity” through a copy-and-paste process, with balances increasing on-screen. Small withdrawals may be processed to build confidence, but larger withdrawals often become restricted, delayed, or subject to additional fees and conditions. This structure closely mirrors known high-risk and Ponzi-style operations.

The promoter narrative you’ve seen — particularly in the transcript — is a clear attempt to redirect attention:

Blaming “scam bloggers” and critics for the warnings
Encouraging people to deposit funds and “try it for themselves”
Dismissing independent research tools like AI because they surface negative information

These are not signs of transparency. They are methods used to reduce scrutiny and keep new deposits flowing.

A legitimate platform does not need to:

Continuously rotate domains
Rely on private chat apps for access
Dismiss regulatory warnings
Encourage blind deposits as a form of “testing”

The warning you are seeing is one of several indicators that something is wrong.

What you do next matters.

Take the warning seriously. Do not ignore it and proceed without understanding the risks. Conduct independent research using multiple sources, including official regulator websites. If you are already involved, stop depositing further funds, keep records of all transactions, and consider reporting the activity to your local financial authority.

BG Wealth Sharing is being presented as a sophisticated trading platform. The evidence suggests something very different.

Stay cautious.

#BGWealthSharing #ScamAlert #DSJExchange #CryptoScam
